offer_letter.markdown:
# Offer of employment — Regional Manager: Fleet

## 1. Our offer to you

Dear {{employee.full_name}}, we are pleased to offer you the job of Regional Manager: Fleet at Absa Group. This is a permanent position. You will start on 1 December 2026. Your place of work is Johannesburg, head office.

## 2. Your role

You will lead regional sales and customer growth for AVMS. You will build a pipeline across Corporate, SME and Public Sector markets, and lead the team through the full sales lifecycle. You will also own customer retention, portfolio growth and profitability for the region. You will lead, coach and performance-manage a regional team of consultants, and work with Credit, Risk, Product, Operations, Finance, Legal and Customer Relations teams.

## 3. Pay and hours

Your basic salary is R18,000.00 per month. We pay monthly on the 25th by EFT. We will deduct PAYE and UIF of 1%. You will work 40 hours a week, 8 hours a day, 5 days a week, Monday to Friday from 08:00 to 17:00, with a meal break of 60 minutes.

## 4. Probation and leave

Your first 3 months are a probationary period. You get 15 working days of paid annual leave in each 12-month leave cycle. You get 30 days' paid sick leave in every 36-month cycle, 3 days' family responsibility leave a year, at least 4 consecutive months' maternity leave, and 10 consecutive days' parental leave.

## 5. Next steps

This offer stays open until 30 November 2026. Please send us your ID and your qualifications. If you have any questions, write to hr@example.co.za.

## 6. Acceptance

If you accept this offer, please sign and return this letter: {{employee.full_name}}, {{date_signed}}.

# Contract of employment — Regional Manager: Fleet

## 1. Parties

This contract of employment is entered into between Absa Group, of 1 Main Road, Johannesburg (the Employer), and {{employee.full_name}}, identity number {{employee.id_number}}, of {{employee.address}} (the Employee).

## 2. Position and duties

The Employer appoints the Employee as Regional Manager: Fleet. The Employee's duties include: Translate the AVMS strategy into a regional sales and customer growth plan with clear segment, production, revenue and profitability priorities.; Build and maintain a balanced regional pipeline across Corporate, SME and Public Sector markets through proactive prospecting, networking, referrals and strategic partnerships.; Lead the team through the full sales lifecycle, including needs analysis, solution design, pricing, proposal development, negotiation, closure and implementation handover.; Achieve regional new business production, revenue, margin and market-share objectives within approved pricing, credit and risk parameters.; Own the health, retention and growth of the regional customer portfolio with the same level of focus as new business acquisition.; Implement a structured customer engagement model, including relationship plans, regular business reviews, service performance reviews and executive engagement for priority customers.; Identify and convert cross-sell, upsell, renewal and fleet expansion opportunities to increase customer share of wallet across AVMS products and value-added services.; Monitor customer satisfaction, complaints, service risks and early-warning indicators; coordinate timely service recovery and root-cause resolution to prevent attrition.; Maintain clear retention and growth plans for customers at risk, strategic accounts and high-potential portfolios.; Lead, coach and performance-manage a regional team of consultants accountable for acquisition, relationship management, retention and portfolio growth.; Allocate customer portfolios, prospects and regional opportunities to ensure clear ownership, appropriate capacity and balanced coverage.; Set individual and team targets and maintain a disciplined management rhythm covering pipeline, customer plans, renewals, service issues, wallet-growth opportunities and forecast accuracy.; Build capability in consultative selling, fleet and leasing solutions, commercial acumen, negotiation, customer engagement and service recovery.; Create a high-performance, customer-led culture with clear accountability, collaboration and succession planning.; Maintain a consolidated regional view of pipeline, portfolio performance, customer profitability, retention risk, wallet growth and service trends.; Use customer, operational and financial insights to prioritise interventions and implement corrective action where performance is below plan.; Ensure accurate forecasting, CRM discipline, management reporting and escalation of material commercial or customer risks.; Balance customer outcomes, commercial returns and risk when making regional decisions.; Coordinate Credit, Risk, Product, Operations, Finance, Legal and Customer Relations stakeholders to deliver integrated customer solutions and resolve regional delivery constraints.; Ensure seamless onboarding and implementation of new customers, with clear handover, service commitments and accountability.; Represent the voice of the customer in product, process and service-improvement forums and provide market intelligence to shape AVMS propositions.; Ensure adherence to Absa policies, sales governance, delegated authorities and applicable regulatory requirements.; Maintain complete and accurate approvals, customer records and deal documentation throughout the customer lifecycle.; Manage customer information in accordance with POPIA and relevant legislation and promptly escalate conduct, service, operational and reputational risks.. The Employer may reasonably require the Employee to perform other duties consistent with the position.

## 3. Commencement

Employment commences on 1 December 2026 on a permanent basis.

## 4. Probation

The first 3 month(s) of employment are a probationary period during which the Employer will assess the Employee's performance against the requirements of the position and give reasonable evaluation, instruction, training, guidance or counselling where needed. Confirmation, extension or termination at the end of probation will follow a fair procedure.

## 5. Place of work

The Employee's place of work is Johannesburg, head office.

## 6. Hours of work

The Employee's ordinary hours of work are 40 hours per week, 8 hours per day over 5 days per week (Mon–Fri 08:00–17:00). A meal interval of 60 minutes is taken after no more than five hours of continuous work. The Employee is entitled to a daily rest period of at least 12 consecutive hours and a weekly rest period of at least 36 consecutive hours.

## 7. Remuneration

The Employee will be paid R18,000.00 per month (basic salary), equivalent to R103.85 per ordinary hour, payable monthly on the 25th by EFT. No other cash payments are payable. No payments in kind are made.

## 8. Overtime

Overtime is worked only by agreement and may not exceed ten hours in any week. Overtime is paid at 1.5 times the Employee's ordinary hourly wage, or, by agreement, compensated with paid time off. Work on a Sunday is paid at double the ordinary wage (or one and a half times if the Employee ordinarily works on Sundays), and work on a public holiday at double the ordinary wage.

## 9. Deductions

The following deductions will be made from the Employee's remuneration: PAYE; UIF 1%. No other deduction will be made without the Employee's written agreement in respect of a specific debt, or as required by law, a court order or an arbitration award.

## 10. Leave

The Employee is entitled to 15 working days of paid annual leave per annual leave cycle of 12 months, to be taken at a time agreed with the Employer and not later than six months after the end of the cycle. Sick leave: 30 days' paid sick leave in every 36-month cycle (during the first six months, one day for every 26 days worked); a medical certificate may be required for absences of more than two consecutive days or on more than two occasions in eight weeks. Maternity leave: at least 4 consecutive months. Parental leave: 10 consecutive days. Adoption and commissioning parental leave as provided in the Act. Family responsibility leave: 3 days' paid leave per year once employed for longer than four months and for at least four days a week.

## 11. Termination and notice

Either party may terminate this contract on written notice of one week if the employee has been employed for six months or less; two weeks if employed for more than six months but not more than one year; four weeks if employed for more than one year. Notice may not be given during any period of leave. Nothing in this clause prevents the Employer from terminating employment summarily for a fair reason following a fair procedure, or the parties from agreeing to waive notice.

## 12. Bargaining council or sectoral determination

No bargaining council agreement or sectoral determination applies to the Employer's business.

## 13. Confidentiality

The Employee will not, during or after employment, disclose or use any confidential information of the Employer, its clients or suppliers, except as required to perform the Employee's duties or by law.

## 14. Other documents

No other documents form part of this contract.

## 15. General

This contract records the whole agreement between the parties on its subject; any amendment must be in writing and signed by both parties. Where any term is less favourable to the Employee than the Basic Conditions of Employment Act or an applicable sectoral determination or collective agreement, the more favourable provision applies. The Employer will keep these particulars for three years after termination and will explain them to the Employee on request.

## 16. Signatures

For the Employer: {{employer.signatory}}  ____________________

The Employee: {{employee.full_name}}  ____________________

plain_language.explanation: This says who the agreement is between. The employer is Absa Group at 1 Main Road, Johannesburg. You are the employee, named with your identity number and your address.

You are appointed as Regional Manager: Fleet. Your duties are listed in full, covering regional sales and growth plans, pipeline building across Corporate, SME and Public Sector markets, leading the sales lifecycle, hitting production, revenue, margin and market-share targets, customer retention and growth, cross-sell and upsell, service recovery, leading and coaching a regional team, setting targets, reporting and forecasting, CRM discipline, working with Credit, Risk, Product, Operations, Finance, Legal and Customer Relations, onboarding new customers, giving market intelligence, following Absa policies, sales governance, delegated authorities and regulations, keeping accurate records, and handling customer information under POPIA. The employer may also reasonably ask you to do other duties that fit this position.
Your employment starts on 1 December 2026. The job is permanent, so it has no end date.

Your first 3 months are a probationary period. During this time the employer will assess your performance against the job requirements and give you reasonable evaluation, instruction, training, guidance or counselling if you need it. At the end of probation the employer may confirm, extend or end your employment, using a fair procedure.
You will work at Johannesburg, head office. That is your place of work under this contract.

You work 40 hours a week, 8 hours a day, over 5 days, Monday to Friday from 08:00 to 17:00. You take a meal break of 60 minutes after no more than five hours of continuous work. You also get a daily rest period of at least 12 continuous hours and a weekly rest period of at least 36 continuous hours.

You are paid R18,000.00 per month as basic salary, which works out to R103.85 for each ordinary hour. Payment is made monthly on the 25th by EFT. No other cash payments and no payments in kind are made.

You only work overtime if you agree to it, and it cannot be more than ten hours in any week. Overtime is paid at 1.5 times your ordinary hourly wage, or you can agree to take paid time off instead. Sunday work is paid at double your ordinary wage (or one and a half times if you normally work Sundays), and public holiday work is paid at double.

The employer will deduct PAYE and UIF of 1% from your pay. No other deduction may be made unless you agree in writing for a specific debt, or the law, a court order or an arbitration award requires it.

You get 15 working days of paid annual leave in each 12-month cycle, taken at a time agreed with the employer and no later than six months after the cycle ends. You get 30 days' paid sick leave in every 36-month cycle; in your first six months you get one day for every 26 days worked, and a medical certificate may be asked for if you are off more than two days in a row or more than twice in eight weeks. Maternity leave is at least 4 consecutive months, parental leave is 10 consecutive days, adoption and commissioning parental leave follow the Act, and family responsibility leave is 3 paid days a year once you have worked longer than four months and work at least four days a week.

Either you or the employer can end the contract with written notice: one week if you have worked six months or less, two weeks if more than six months but not more than one year, and four weeks if more than one year. Notice cannot be given while you are on leave. The employer may still dismiss you immediately for a fair reason using a fair procedure, and both sides can agree to skip notice.
No bargaining council agreement applies to the employer's business. No sectoral determination applies either. So your terms come from this contract.

You may not share or use the employer's confidential information, or that of its clients or suppliers. This applies while you work there and after you leave. The only exceptions are when you need it to do your job or when the law requires it.
No other documents form part of this contract. Only what is written in this contract applies.

This contract is the whole agreement on its subject, and any change must be in writing and signed by both you and the employer. If any term gives you less than the Basic Conditions of Employment Act, a sectoral determination or a collective agreement, the better term applies. The employer will keep these particulars for three years after your employment ends and will explain them to you if you ask.
This is the signature block. It records the place and the date of signing. The employer's signatory signs for Absa Group, and you sign as the employee.
